C=======================================================================
C  ICE 0.51  --  recovered source, module 0C4D
C  USNO Compressed Ephemeris: parameter file, ephemeris files,
C  decompression of the packed Chebyshev residuals and evaluation.
C
C  Model: each body's barycentric position is a Chebyshev series over
C  an interval equal to (about) its orbital period.  For Mercury..Mars
C  and the Moon a reference orbit (PARAM.DAT, CA/CB) is rotated into
C  place and the residual series from EPHnn.DAT is added; the outer
C  planets and the Sun use the residual series alone.  The residual
C  coefficients are stored as integers in a variable-width packing
C  (32, 24, 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1 bit fields), see UNPACK.
C
C  Two far COMMON blocks hold the data (segments 2000 and 2109 of the
C  original); names are invented, layout is the original one.
C=======================================================================
C
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
C  Block data for the ephemeris commons
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
      BLOCK DATA EPHBD
      DOUBLE PRECISION TB(2), TE(2), XMU, EMRAT, CC(41,3,11)
      INTEGER*4 IDATE(30), JHDR(11,2), IDAT(10000,2), IPTR(400,2),
     &          IHDR(21,2), NLAST(11), NREF, IB
      LOGICAL FIRST
      COMMON /EPHBUF/ TB, TE, XMU, EMRAT, CC, IDATE, JHDR, IDAT, IPTR,
     &                IHDR, NLAST, NREF, IB, FIRST
      DATA EMRAT / 0.01230002D0 /
      DATA FIRST / .TRUE. /
      END
C
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
C  SOLSYS   [0C4D:0008]  position and velocity of a body
C           TJD    TDB Julian date
C           NB     body: 1 Mercury .. 9 Pluto, 10 Sun, 11 Moon
C           IORIG  0 = solar-system barycentre, 1 = centre of the Sun
C           POS    position, AU;  VEL velocity, AU/day
C           IERR   0 ok, 1 date before / 2 date after the ephemeris
C                  files, 3 bad argument
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
      SUBROUTINE SOLSYS (TJD, NB, IORIG, POS, VEL, IERR)
      DOUBLE PRECISION TJD, POS(3), VEL(3)
      INTEGER*4 NB, IORIG, IERR
      DOUBLE PRECISION T0, PER(11), PB(11), PC(11), E1(4), E2(4),
     &     SC(11), E3(5), F1(5), F2(5), CA(42,5), CB(42,5),
     &     START(11), SPAN(11), XM1, XM2, XM3, XM4, CE, SE
      INTEGER*4 NCREF(5), NX(11), IREC(11)
      COMMON /EPHPAR/ T0, PER, PB, PC, E1, E2, SC, E3, F1, F2, CA, CB,
     &     START, SPAN, XM1, XM2, XM3, XM4, CE, SE, NCREF, NX, IREC
      DOUBLE PRECISION TB(2), TE(2), XMU, EMRAT, CC(41,3,11)
      INTEGER*4 IDATE(30), JHDR(11,2), IDAT(10000,2), IPTR(400,2),
     &          IHDR(21,2), NLAST(11), NREF, IB
      LOGICAL FIRST
      COMMON /EPHBUF/ TB, TE, XMU, EMRAT, CC, IDATE, JHDR, IDAT, IPTR,
     &                IHDR, NLAST, NREF, IB, FIRST
      DOUBLE PRECISION FM
      INTEGER*4 IEARTH, IMOON, ISUN, K0, K1, NCOF, I, IPOS
      LOGICAL LFLAG
      SAVE
      IEARTH = 3
      IMOON = 11
      ISUN = 10
      K0 = 0
      NCOF = 41
      K1 = 1
      IF (NB .LE. 0 .OR. NB .GE. 12) GO TO 90
      IF (IORIG .NE. 0 .AND. IORIG .NE. 1) GO TO 90
      IERR = 0
C
C     first call: read PARAM.DAT, invalidate everything
      IF (FIRST) THEN
         XMU = 1.D0 / (1.D0/EMRAT + 1.D0)
         IB = 2
         TB(1) = 1.D10
         TB(2) = 1.D10
         DO 10 I = 1, 11
            IREC(I) = 0
            START(I) = 1.D10
            SPAN(I) = 1.D10
   10    CONTINUE
         CALL PARAMS (NREF, IDATE)
         FIRST = .FALSE.
      END IF
C
C     coefficients for body NB current?  if not, make sure one of the
C     two ephemeris-file buffers covers TJD, then decode the interval
      IF (START(NB) .GT. TJD .OR. START(NB)+SPAN(NB) .LT. TJD) THEN
         IF (TB(IB) .GT. TJD .OR. TE(IB) .LT. TJD) THEN
            IB = 3.2 - IB
            IF (TB(IB) .GT. TJD .OR. TE(IB) .LT. TJD) THEN
               CALL EPHRD (TJD, IDATE, IHDR(1,IB), IPTR(1,IB),
     &              IDAT(1,IB), TB(IB), TE(IB), JHDR(1,IB), IERR)
               IF (IERR .NE. 0) THEN
                  IB = 3.2 - IB
                  RETURN
               END IF
            END IF
         END IF
         CALL LOCATE (NB, NREF, TJD, LFLAG, IPOS, IHDR(1,IB),
     &        IPTR(1,IB), TB(IB), TE(IB), JHDR(1,IB))
         CALL COEFS (NB, NREF, IDAT(IPOS,IB), LFLAG, CC(1,1,NB),
     &        NLAST(NB))
      END IF
C
C     the Earth needs the Moon and the Moon needs the Earth-Moon
C     barycentre (series 3 is the barycentre)
      IF (NB .EQ. 3 .OR. NB .EQ. 11) THEN
         IF (NB .NE. 3) THEN
            IF (START(3) .GT. TJD .OR. START(3)+SPAN(3) .LT. TJD) THEN
               CALL LOCATE (IEARTH, NREF, TJD, LFLAG, IPOS, IHDR(1,IB),
     &              IPTR(1,IB), TB(IB), TE(IB), JHDR(1,IB))
               CALL COEFS (IEARTH, NREF, IDAT(IPOS,IB), LFLAG,
     &              CC(1,1,3), NLAST(3))
            END IF
         END IF
         IF (START(11) .GT. TJD .OR. START(11)+SPAN(11) .LT. TJD) THEN
            CALL LOCATE (IMOON, NREF, TJD, LFLAG, IPOS, IHDR(1,IB),
     &           IPTR(1,IB), TB(IB), TE(IB), JHDR(1,IB))
            CALL COEFS (IMOON, NREF, IDAT(IPOS,IB), LFLAG,
     &           CC(1,1,11), NLAST(11))
         END IF
      END IF
      IF (IORIG .NE. 0) THEN
         IF (START(10) .GT. TJD .OR. START(10)+SPAN(10) .LT. TJD) THEN
            CALL LOCATE (ISUN, NREF, TJD, LFLAG, IPOS, IHDR(1,IB),
     &           IPTR(1,IB), TB(IB), TE(IB), JHDR(1,IB))
            CALL COEFS (ISUN, NREF, IDAT(IPOS,IB), LFLAG,
     &           CC(1,1,10), NLAST(10))
         END IF
      END IF
C
C     position
      CALL CHEBEV (NB, NREF, K0, NCOF, NLAST(NB), TJD, 0.D0, POS,
     &     1.D0, CC(1,1,NB), POS)
      IF (NB .EQ. 3 .OR. NB .EQ. 11) THEN
         IF (NB .NE. 3) THEN
            FM = 1.D0 - XMU
            CALL CHEBEV (IEARTH, NREF, K0, NCOF, NLAST(3), TJD, FM,
     &           POS, 1.D0, CC(1,1,3), POS)
         ELSE
            FM = -XMU
            CALL CHEBEV (IMOON, NREF, K0, NCOF, NLAST(11), TJD, 1.D0,
     &           POS, FM, CC(1,1,11), POS)
         END IF
      END IF
      IF (IORIG .NE. 0) CALL CHEBEV (ISUN, NREF, K0, NCOF, NLAST(10),
     &     TJD, 1.D0, POS, -1.D0, CC(1,1,10), POS)
C
C     velocity
      CALL CHEBEV (NB, NREF, K1, NCOF, NLAST(NB), TJD, 0.D0, VEL,
     &     1.D0, CC(1,1,NB), VEL)
      IF (NB .EQ. 3 .OR. NB .EQ. 11) THEN
         IF (NB .NE. 3) THEN
            FM = 1.D0 - XMU
            CALL CHEBEV (IEARTH, NREF, K1, NCOF, NLAST(3), TJD, FM,
     &           VEL, 1.D0, CC(1,1,3), VEL)
         ELSE
            FM = -XMU
            CALL CHEBEV (IMOON, NREF, K1, NCOF, NLAST(11), TJD, 1.D0,
     &           VEL, FM, CC(1,1,11), VEL)
         END IF
      END IF
      IF (IORIG .NE. 0) CALL CHEBEV (ISUN, NREF, K1, NCOF, NLAST(10),
     &     TJD, 1.D0, VEL, -1.D0, CC(1,1,10), VEL)
      CLOSE (15)
      RETURN
   90 IERR = 3
      RETURN
      END
C
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
C  PARAMS   [0C4D:1465]  read PARAM.DAT (unit 20): file date table,
C           per-body interval lengths, orientation elements and the
C           reference-orbit series.  NREF returns the number of bodies
C           (1..NREF) that have a reference orbit (4).
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
      SUBROUTINE PARAMS (NREF, IDATE)
      INTEGER*4 NREF, IDATE(30)
      DOUBLE PRECISION T0, PER(11), PB(11), PC(11), E1(4), E2(4),
     &     SC(11), E3(5), F1(5), F2(5), CA(42,5), CB(42,5),
     &     START(11), SPAN(11), XM1, XM2, XM3, XM4, CE, SE
      INTEGER*4 NCREF(5), NX(11), IREC(11)
      COMMON /EPHPAR/ T0, PER, PB, PC, E1, E2, SC, E3, F1, F2, CA, CB,
     &     START, SPAN, XM1, XM2, XM3, XM4, CE, SE, NCREF, NX, IREC
      DOUBLE PRECISION OBL
      CHARACTER*4096 ICEFILE
      CHARACTER*30 NAME
      INTEGER*4 I, J, NB, NC, NXX
      LOGICAL LEX
      SAVE
      OBL = 0.4090928D0
      CE = DCOS (OBL)
      SE = DSIN (OBL)
      GO TO 20
   10 WRITE (*,*) 'File PARAM.DAT not found on active disk.'
      PAUSE 'Insert correct disk and press "Enter" when ready.'
   20 INQUIRE (FILE=ICEFILE('PARAM.DAT'), EXIST=LEX)
      IF (.NOT. LEX) GO TO 10
      OPEN (20, FILE=ICEFILE('PARAM.DAT'), FORM='UNFORMATTED')
      DO 50 I = 1, 11
         IF (I .EQ. 1) READ (20) IDATE
         READ (20, END=99) NAME, NB, NREF, NC, NXX
         IF (NREF .GE. NB) NCREF(NB) = NC
         IF (NB .EQ. 11) NCREF(5) = NC
         NX(NB) = NXX
         IREC(NB) = I
         READ (20) T0, PER(NB)
         READ (20) PB(NB), PC(NB), SC(NB)
         IF (NB .LT. 11 .AND. NREF .LT. NB) GO TO 50
         IF (NB .EQ. 11) GO TO 40
         READ (20) E1(NB), E2(NB), E3(NB)
   30    READ (20) F1(NB), F2(NB)
         READ (20) (CA(J,NB), J = 1, NC+1)
         READ (20) (CB(J,NB), J = 1, NC+1)
         GO TO 50
C        the Moon's reference orbit is kept in slot 5
   40    READ (20) XM1, XM2, XM3
         READ (20) XM4, E3(5)
         NB = 5
         GO TO 30
   50 CONTINUE
   99 RETURN
      END
C
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
C  EPHRD    [0C4D:17EB]  load the ephemeris file EPHnn.DAT that covers
C           TJD (units 21..44): header, pointer table, packed data.
C           IDATE(K)/100 is the starting Julian date of file K.
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
      SUBROUTINE EPHRD (TJD, IDATE, IHDR, IPTR, IDAT, TBEG, TEND,
     &                  JHDR, IERR)
      DOUBLE PRECISION TJD, TBEG, TEND
      INTEGER*4 IDATE(30), IHDR(21), IPTR(*), IDAT(*), JHDR(11), IERR
      DOUBLE PRECISION D1, D2
      INTEGER*4 I, J, K, NUP, NDAT
      LOGICAL LEX
      CHARACTER*4096 ICEFILE
      CHARACTER*9 FNAME(24)
      SAVE
      DATA FNAME / 'EPH01.DAT', 'EPH02.DAT', 'EPH03.DAT', 'EPH04.DAT',
     &             'EPH05.DAT', 'EPH06.DAT', 'EPH07.DAT', 'EPH08.DAT',
     &             'EPH09.DAT', 'EPH10.DAT', 'EPH11.DAT', 'EPH12.DAT',
     &             'EPH13.DAT', 'EPH14.DAT', 'EPH15.DAT', 'EPH16.DAT',
     &             'EPH17.DAT', 'EPH18.DAT', 'EPH19.DAT', 'EPH20.DAT',
     &             'EPH21.DAT', 'EPH22.DAT', 'EPH23.DAT', 'EPH24.DAT' /
      D1 = IDATE(1) * 0.01D0
      D2 = IDATE(30) * 0.01D0
      IF (D1 .GT. TJD .OR. D2 .LT. TJD) THEN
         IERR = 2
         IF (TJD .LT. D1 + 0.01D0) IERR = 1
         RETURN
      END IF
      DO 10 I = 1, 29
         K = I
         TEND = IDATE(I+1) * 0.01D0
         IF (TEND .GE. TJD) GO TO 20
   10 CONTINUE
   20 TBEG = IDATE(K) * 0.01D0
      GO TO 40
   30 WRITE (*,*) 'Ephemeris file ', FNAME(K), ' not found on ',
     &            'active disk.'
      PAUSE 'Insert correct disk and press "Enter" when ready.'
   40 INQUIRE (FILE=ICEFILE(FNAME(K)), EXIST=LEX)
      IF (.NOT. LEX) GO TO 30
      OPEN (K+20, FILE=ICEFILE(FNAME(K)), FORM='UNFORMATTED')
      READ (K+20) IHDR, JHDR
      NUP = IHDR(IHDR(1)) + 1
      DO 50 I = 1, NUP, 64
         READ (K+20) (IPTR(J), J = I, I+63)
   50 CONTINUE
      NDAT = IPTR(NUP) - 1
      DO 60 I = 1, NDAT, 64
         READ (K+20) (IDAT(J), J = I, I+63)
   60 CONTINUE
      CLOSE (K+20)
      RETURN
      END
C
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
C  LOCATE   [0C4D:1C87]  find the interval of body NB that contains
C           TJD in the loaded ephemeris file; sets START(NB), SPAN(NB),
C           IPOS (index of its packed record in IDAT) and LFLAG
C           (.TRUE. if the record is a residual to a reference orbit)
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
      SUBROUTINE LOCATE (NB, NREF, TJD, LFLAG, IPOS, IHDR, IPTR,
     &                   TBEG, TEND, JHDR)
      INTEGER*4 NB, NREF, IPOS, IHDR(*), IPTR(*), JHDR(*)
      DOUBLE PRECISION TJD, TBEG, TEND
      LOGICAL LFLAG
      DOUBLE PRECISION T0, PER(11), PB(11), PC(11), E1(4), E2(4),
     &     SC(11), E3(5), F1(5), F2(5), CA(42,5), CB(42,5),
     &     START(11), SPAN(11), XM1, XM2, XM3, XM4, CE, SE
      INTEGER*4 NCREF(5), NX(11), IREC(11)
      COMMON /EPHPAR/ T0, PER, PB, PC, E1, E2, SC, E3, F1, F2, CA, CB,
     &     START, SPAN, XM1, XM2, XM3, XM4, CE, SE, NCREF, NX, IREC
      DOUBLE PRECISION TS
      INTEGER*4 K, N
      SAVE
      IF (IREC(NB) .LE. 1) THEN
         K = 1
      ELSE
         K = IHDR(IREC(NB)) + 1
      END IF
      IF (NB .GT. NREF .AND. NB .NE. 11) THEN
C        intervals start at TBEG
         LFLAG = .FALSE.
         N = (TJD - TBEG) / PER(NB)
         IF (K + N .GE. IHDR(IREC(NB)+1)) N = IHDR(IREC(NB)+1) - K
         K = K + N
         START(NB) = PER(NB) * N + TBEG
      ELSE
C        first (partial) interval ends at TS
         TS = JHDR(NB) * 1.D-5 + TBEG
         IF (TJD .LT. TS) THEN
            LFLAG = .FALSE.
            START(NB) = TBEG
            SPAN(NB) = TS - TBEG
            GO TO 10
         END IF
         N = (TJD - TS) / PER(NB)
         LFLAG = .TRUE.
         IF (K + N + 1 .GE. IHDR(IREC(NB)+1)) THEN
            N = IHDR(IREC(NB)+1) - K - 1
            LFLAG = .FALSE.
         END IF
         K = K + N + 1
         START(NB) = PER(NB) * N + TS
      END IF
      SPAN(NB) = DMIN1 (TEND - START(NB), PER(NB))
   10 IPOS = IPTR(K)
      RETURN
      END
C
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
C  COEFS    [0C4D:2030]  decode the Chebyshev coefficients of body NB
C           for the current interval into CC(41,3) (equatorial frame).
C           Residual series are unpacked from IDAT; when LFLAG is set
C           the reference orbit is added in its orbital plane, then
C           the plane (P,Q = tan(i/2) sin/cos node) is rotated into
C           place.  NLAST = last significant coefficient.
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
      SUBROUTINE COEFS (NB, NREF, IDAT, LFLAG, CC, NLAST)
      INTEGER*4 NB, NREF, IDAT(*), NLAST
      LOGICAL LFLAG
      DOUBLE PRECISION CC(41,3)
      DOUBLE PRECISION T0, PER(11), PB(11), PC(11), E1(4), E2(4),
     &     SC(11), E3(5), F1(5), F2(5), CA(42,5), CB(42,5),
     &     START(11), SPAN(11), XM1, XM2, XM3, XM4, CE, SE
      INTEGER*4 NCREF(5), NX(11), IREC(11)
      COMMON /EPHPAR/ T0, PER, PB, PC, E1, E2, SC, E3, F1, F2, CA, CB,
     &     START, SPAN, XM1, XM2, XM3, XM4, CE, SE, NCREF, NX, IREC
      DOUBLE PRECISION ANG, CA1, SA1, Y(3), P, Q, R(3,3), TC, DEN,
     &     S, PP, QQ, X1, X2, X3
      INTEGER*4 IX, I, KMAX, N41
      SAVE
      N41 = 41
      IF (.NOT. LFLAG) THEN
         KMAX = 0
         P = PB(NB)
         Q = PC(NB)
         CALL UNPACK (IDAT, N41, SC(NB), CC)
      ELSE
C        time of mid-interval, thousands of Julian years from T0
         TC = (PER(NB)*0.5D0 + START(NB) - T0) / 365250.D0
         IF (NB .EQ. 11) THEN
            P = DCOS (XM4*TC + XM2) * (XM3*TC + XM1)
            Q = DSIN (XM4*TC + XM2) * (XM3*TC + XM1)
            IX = 5
         ELSE
            P = E1(NB)*TC + PB(NB)
            Q = E2(NB)*TC + PC(NB)
            IX = NB
         END IF
         ANG = F2(IX)*TC + F1(IX)
         CA1 = DCOS (ANG)
         SA1 = DSIN (ANG)
         CALL UNPACK (IDAT, N41, E3(IX), CC)
         KMAX = NCREF(IX) + 1
         DO 10 I = 1, KMAX
            CC(I,1) = CC(I,1) + CA1*CA(I,IX) - SA1*CB(I,IX)
            CC(I,2) = CC(I,2) + CA1*CB(I,IX) + SA1*CA(I,IX)
   10    CONTINUE
      END IF
C     rotation matrix from the orbital plane
      QQ = Q*Q
      PP = P*P
      S = PP + QQ
      DEN = 1.D0 / (S + 1.D0)
      R(1,3) = DEN*Q*2.D0
      R(2,3) = -(P*DEN*2.D0)
      R(3,3) = (1.D0 - S)*DEN
      R(1,1) = (PP - QQ + 1.D0)*DEN
      R(2,1) = P*Q*DEN*2.D0
      R(3,1) = -R(1,3)
      R(1,2) = R(2,1)
      R(2,2) = (QQ - PP + 1.D0)*DEN
      R(3,2) = P*DEN*2.D0
      NLAST = 0
      KMAX = MAX0 (KMAX, NX(NB)+1)
      DO 20 I = 1, KMAX
         X3 = CC(I,3)
         X2 = CC(I,2)
         X1 = CC(I,1)
         Y(1) = R(1,1)*X1 + R(1,2)*X2 + R(1,3)*X3
         Y(2) = R(2,1)*X1 + R(2,2)*X2 + R(2,3)*X3
         Y(3) = R(3,1)*X1 + R(3,2)*X2 + R(3,3)*X3
         IF (DABS(Y(1)) + DABS(Y(2)) + DABS(Y(3)) .GE. 1.D-14)
     &      NLAST = I
         CC(I,1) = Y(1)
         IF (NB .EQ. 11) THEN
C           the Moon's series are ecliptic
            CC(I,2) = CE*Y(2) - SE*Y(3)
            CC(I,3) = SE*Y(2) + CE*Y(3)
         ELSE
            CC(I,2) = Y(2)
            CC(I,3) = Y(3)
         END IF
   20 CONTINUE
      RETURN
      END
C
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
C  CHEBEV   [0C4D:275B]  evaluate the series of body NB at TJD:
C           K = 0 position, K = 1 velocity (d/dt);
C           R(J) = S*Y(J) + F*series(J), J = 1..3
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
      SUBROUTINE CHEBEV (NB, NREF, K, NC, N, TJD, S, Y, F, C, R)
      INTEGER*4 NB, NREF, K, NC, N
      DOUBLE PRECISION TJD, S, Y(3), F, C(NC,3), R(3)
      DOUBLE PRECISION T0, PER(11), PB(11), PC(11), E1(4), E2(4),
     &     SC(11), E3(5), F1(5), F2(5), CA(42,5), CB(42,5),
     &     START(11), SPAN(11), XM1, XM2, XM3, XM4, CE, SE
      INTEGER*4 NCREF(5), NX(11), IREC(11)
      COMMON /EPHPAR/ T0, PER, PB, PC, E1, E2, SC, E3, F1, F2, CA, CB,
     &     START, SPAN, XM1, XM2, XM3, XM4, CE, SE, NCREF, NX, IREC
      DOUBLE PRECISION HALF, TMID, X, V, FAC0, FAC1
      INTEGER*4 J
      LOGICAL LFONE, LFMONE, LSZERO, LSONE
      SAVE
      HALF = SPAN(NB) * 0.5D0
      TMID = START(NB) + HALF
C     the series are fitted over 1.1 times the interval (not the Moon)
      IF (NB .NE. 11) HALF = 1.1D0 * HALF
      X = -((TJD - TMID) / HALF)
      IF (K .EQ. 0) FAC0 = F
      IF (K .EQ. 1) FAC1 = -(F / HALF)
      LFONE = .FALSE.
      LFMONE = .FALSE.
      LSONE = .FALSE.
      LSZERO = .FALSE.
      IF (DABS(F - 1.D0) .LT. 1.D-13) LFONE = .TRUE.
      IF (DABS(F + 1.D0) .LT. 1.D-13) LFMONE = .TRUE.
      IF (DABS(S) .LT. 1.D-13) LSZERO = .TRUE.
      IF (DABS(S - 1.D0) .LT. 1.D-13) LSONE = .TRUE.
      DO 10 J = 1, 3
         IF (K .EQ. 1) THEN
            CALL CHEBD (X, C(1,J), N, V)
            V = FAC1 * V
         ELSE
            CALL CHEB (X, C(1,J), N, V)
            IF (.NOT. LFONE) THEN
               IF (LFMONE) THEN
                  V = -V
               ELSE
                  V = FAC0 * V
               END IF
            END IF
         END IF
         IF (LSONE) THEN
            R(J) = Y(J) + V
         ELSE IF (LSZERO) THEN
            R(J) = V
         ELSE
            R(J) = Y(J)*S + V
         END IF
   10 CONTINUE
      RETURN
      END
C
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
C  UNPACK   [0C4D:2AD9]  unpack the residual coefficients of one
C           interval: IDAT -> C(NC,3) * SCALE.
C           Per component a header word holds six base-40 digits:
C           KF(6) 32-bit words, KF(5) 24-bit values (M of them paired
C           with an 8-bit value in the low byte), then KF(4), KF(3),
C           KF(2), KF(1) values of 16, 8, 4 and 2 bits packed into
C           16-bit fields, two per word, after all three components.
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
      SUBROUTINE UNPACK (IDAT, NC, SCALE, C)
      INTEGER*4 IDAT(*), NC
      DOUBLE PRECISION SCALE, C(NC,3)
      INTEGER*4 NBW, IR4, IR3, IR2, IR1, IA, I, L, J, IS, I2, KK, IP,
     &     LO(3), KF(6,3), IBIAS, NBITS, M, NG(4,3), HI(3), IB(200),
     &     IPT(16), K1
      SAVE
      DATA IPT / 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048,
     &           4096, 8192, 16384, 32768 /
      DO 10 J = 1, 3
         DO 10 I = 1, NC
            C(I,J) = 0.D0
   10 CONTINUE
      IP = 0
      DO 40 J = 1, 3
C        header word: six base-40 counts
         IP = IP + 1
         IA = IABS (IDAT(IP))
         IR1 = MOD (IA, 102400000)
         KF(6,J) = IA / 102400000
         IF (IDAT(IP) .LT. 0) KF(6,J) = KF(6,J) + 20
         IR2 = MOD (IR1, 2560000)
         KF(5,J) = IR1 / 2560000
         IR3 = MOD (IR2, 64000)
         KF(4,J) = IR2 / 64000
         IR4 = MOD (IR3, 1600)
         KF(3,J) = IR3 / 1600
         KF(1,J) = MOD (IR4, 40)
         KF(2,J) = IR4 / 40
C        full 32-bit coefficients
         LO(J) = 1
         HI(J) = KF(6,J)
         DO 20 I = 1, HI(J)
            IP = IP + 1
            C(I,J) = IDAT(IP) * SCALE
   20    CONTINUE
C        24-bit coefficients; the first M carry an 8-bit one as well
         M = MIN0 (KF(5,J), KF(3,J) + KF(2,J) + KF(1,J))
         NG(4,J) = KF(4,J)
         NG(3,J) = MAX0 (KF(3,J) - M, 0)
         NG(2,J) = MAX0 (KF(2,J) - MAX0 (M - KF(3,J), 0), 0)
         NG(1,J) = MAX0 (KF(1,J) - MAX0 (M - KF(3,J) - KF(2,J), 0), 0)
         I2 = KF(6,J) + KF(5,J) + KF(4,J)
         LO(J) = HI(J) + 1
         HI(J) = HI(J) + M
         DO 30 I = LO(J), HI(J)
            IP = IP + 1
            I2 = I2 + 1
            IA = IABS (IDAT(IP))
            IF (IDAT(IP) .GT. 0) THEN
               K1 = IA / 256 - 8388608
            ELSE
               K1 = IA / 256
            END IF
            C(I,J) = K1 * SCALE
            C(I2,J) = (MOD (IA, 256) - 128) * SCALE
   30    CONTINUE
         LO(J) = HI(J) + 1
         HI(J) = HI(J) + KF(5,J) - M
         DO 35 I = LO(J), HI(J)
            IP = IP + 1
            C(I,J) = IDAT(IP) * SCALE
   35    CONTINUE
   40 CONTINUE
C     the remaining small coefficients: 16-bit fields, two per word
      NBITS = 0
      DO 50 J = 1, 3
         NBITS = NBITS + NG(4,J)*8 + NG(3,J)*4 + NG(2,J)*2 + NG(1,J)
   50 CONTINUE
      NBITS = (NBITS + 15) / 16 * 2
      DO 60 L = 2, NBITS, 2
         IP = IP + 1
         IA = IABS (IDAT(IP))
         IF (IDAT(IP) .GE. 0) THEN
            IB(L-1) = IA / 65536
         ELSE
            IB(L-1) = IA / 65536 + 32768
         END IF
         IB(L) = MOD (IA, 65536)
   60 CONTINUE
C     peel off fields of 16, 8, 4, 2 bits
      IS = 17
      L = 1
      DO 90 KK = 1, 4
         NBW = 2 ** (5 - KK)
         IBIAS = 2 ** (NBW - 1)
         DO 80 J = 1, 3
            HI(J) = HI(J) + KF(5-KK,J)
            LO(J) = HI(J) - NG(5-KK,J) + 1
            DO 70 I = LO(J), HI(J)
               IF (NBW + 1 .LT. IS) THEN
                  IS = IS - NBW
                  C(I,J) = (IB(L) / IPT(IS) - IBIAS) * SCALE
                  IB(L) = MOD (IB(L), IPT(IS))
               ELSE
                  C(I,J) = (IB(L) - IBIAS) * SCALE
                  IS = 17
                  L = L + 1
               END IF
   70       CONTINUE
   80    CONTINUE
   90 CONTINUE
      RETURN
      END
C
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
C  CHEB     [0C4D:37BA]  Chebyshev series by Clenshaw's recurrence
C           F = C(1)/2 + SUM C(K+1)*T(K,X),  K = 1..N-1
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
      SUBROUTINE CHEB (X, C, N, F)
      DOUBLE PRECISION X, C(*), F, TWOX, B0, B1, B2
      INTEGER*4 N, J, K
      SAVE
      TWOX = X * 2.D0
      B0 = 0.D0
      B1 = 0.D0
      DO 10 J = 1, N
         K = N - J + 1
         B2 = B1
         B1 = B0
         B0 = C(K) + TWOX * B1 - B2
   10 CONTINUE
      F = (B0 - B2) * 0.5D0
      RETURN
      END
C
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
C  CHEBD    [0C4D:38ED]  derivative (with respect to X) of the series
C           evaluated by CHEB
C-----------------------------------------------------------------------
      SUBROUTINE CHEBD (X, C, N, F)
      DOUBLE PRECISION X, C(*), F, TWOX, D, D1, D2, B0, B1, B2, B2S, TK
      INTEGER*4 N, J, K, NM1
      SAVE
      TWOX = X * 2.D0
      D1 = 0.D0
      D2 = 0.D0
      B1 = 0.D0
      B2 = 0.D0
      NM1 = N - 1
      DO 10 J = 1, NM1
         K = N - J
         TK = 2 * K
         D = TK * C(K+1) + D1
         B0 = D + TWOX * B1 - B2
         B2S = B2
         B2 = B1
         B1 = B0
         D1 = D2
         D2 = D
   10 CONTINUE
      F = (B0 - B2S) * 0.5D0
      RETURN
      END

# Wings of Fury STE: open points

What is still open. Things that are done are not listed.

## To confirm on real hardware (fixed in code, checked in Hatari)

- **HDDRIVER black screen** (fixed in 0.9.0, see `docs/AGT_CHANGES.md`, "The 200 Hz clock"): confirmed in Hatari
  with the HDDRIVER 13.01 demo, not on a real machine with HDDRIVER.
- **Quit: the desktop's own resolution and palette** (0.9.0). To test on the STE and the Mega STE: start from a low
  and from a medium resolution desktop, quit with Ctrl+Q and with "Exit Game" in the load dialog; check resolution,
  colours and mouse pointer. The medium case has not run anywhere.
- **Floppy program started by hand** (0.9.0): on a machine that boots from a hard disk the floppy's AUTO folder is
  not run; started from the desktop the program looks for DATA one folder up. Checked in Hatari with the same
  folder layout on a hard disk folder, not from a floppy.
- **Memory check** (0.9.1): "Not enough free memory. Free: n KB, needed: n KB". Needed at the game's entry:
  1164 KB with the files as they are, 1258 KB with the packed floppy files (the check adds 16 KB for larger level
  bundles: an estimate, only mission 1 was run at the limit). A plain 2 MB STE has 1547 KB there (TOS 2.06:
  1538 KB), a 1 MB one 499 KB.
- **New in 0.9.3**: ships and the own carrier sink 1 px per stage, with the ship's row showing at the waterline
  between the wave crests; pillbox damage in the 1/8 view; the Zero's muzzle flash in the colours of the Amiga's
  exclusive-or; Ctrl+S, F, C, V. Checked in Hatari only.

- **Program and one data archive** (1.0.1): the hard disk version is `WOF.PRG`, `WOF.DAT`, `README.TXT`; the floppy
  `AUTO/WOF.PRG`, `WOF.DAT`, `README.TXT`. To test: both start and load every mission; loading times against the
  build before; the SAVE folder is made on the first start; a `WOF.DAT` that was cut short is reported; a Shift key
  held at the start checks all of it. Checked in Hatari (floppy on TOS 1.62, a hard disk folder, HDDRIVER).
- **Fewer late frames** (1.0.2): the sound mixer writes each stereo side in one pass (same bytes as before, `make
  mixtest`), a carrier bob step copies only the tiles that change, the soldier scans, score digits and random
  numbers are cheaper, and the sound lead no longer grows after a single late frame. Frames over 3 VBLs in the six
  scripted runs in Hatari: 5758 before, 1743 after (sortie 264 to 90, views 360 to 185, combat 790 to 460, crashes
  645 to 401, maps 1609 to 516, soak 1090 to 91). Run 1 on the Mega STE: 96 late frames (1.0.1: 264), the same
  events as Hatari. 1.0.3: the panel redraws only the items that changed (a gauge needle, a digit, a lamp) instead of
  all of them: 1581 in the six runs (sortie 76, views 185, combat 405, crashes 380, maps 472, soak 63). To check on
  the STE and the Mega STE: the run logs, and that the sound is unchanged.

- **Louder sound** (1.0.4): every voice at full scale, as a Paula channel at volume 64 (before: half, so that two
  voices on one side could never overflow); two voices on a side are added with saturation. 6 dB louder on average
  (Hatari, `tests/takeoff_fire`: -25.2 to -19.2 dB), no clipped stretches seen there; `make mixtest` checks it
  against a reference that clips the same way. Mega STE (1.0.4+876eeb8, Scarlett line input): no crackle
  heard; in flight -21 to -24 dB average, peaks at the DMA's full scale (-13.4 dB), 0.01 % of samples there. The
  ST original of Super Cars II measures -18 dB at the same gain: a soft limiter could add 3 to 6 dB. Still to
  check on the STE.

## Known issues

- **Runner text garbled after the run build's exit** (STE, 1.1.0+4f0f466, scripted run 1 ending by itself): the
  runner's "[EXIT]" line shows every other character, in single colours (a 2-plane text layout on the 4-plane
  screen). The run log's `EXITVID` line right after the exit reads low resolution, screen address = `Logbase`, line
  width and fine scroll 0. Ctrl+Q in WOF.PRG on the Mega STE gave a clean runner screen (c330419). Suspect: TOS's
  screen-driver variables left at medium resolution (AGT's restore switches to medium; the run build skips the
  intro's Setscreen calls). Asked the Atari-Dev session for the known fix.

- **A chasing enemy plane does not attack** (deferred, seen in Hatari with 1.0.0+f248896): a plane
  that chases the player gets right behind it but does not fire; it turns round, then follows again, and repeats
  that cycle. Looked at so far: a Zero from an airfield (map d) behind a plane flying straight and level holds 131 px
  and fires until the player goes down, so the fighter's attack works. Missions a, b and c have no airfield and no
  ship: the only enemy planes there are the carrier bombers, which never fire at the player in the original either
  (`zero_bomber`, FUN_1dea4): they go for the carrier, turn round when they are past it or when their timer runs
  out, and slow down when the player is behind them. Open: which mission it was. If it was a bomber, this is the
  original's behaviour; if it was a fighter in a later mission, the case has to be found (turning player, two
  planes and the attack queue, a plane coming head-on).

## Differences from the Amiga still open

- **Enemy ships don't bob** on the waves. The original (measured in vAmiga, map g's ship): the whole
  picture, its guns and parked planes move 1 px up and down with the wave bob (2, 3, 4, 3: a step every 21 ticks; a
  larger value is lower), the wave strip in front stays still, and a sinking ship keeps bobbing. Here only the own
  carrier bobs (three stored copies), and it stops when it sinks. The sinking mechanism could do it (shift = stage +
  bob - 3), but then every ship in view needs its block of own tiles (about 40 KB each) and a redraw every 1.7 s.
- **Ctrl keys:** all of the original's are in (Ctrl+V shows this build's version where the original says
  "Version 1.0"). Ctrl+S, F, C, V have not been run yet. Ctrl+B (a debug trap) is left out on purpose.
- **Sea crash near the carrier:** the orange explosion uses the Amiga's position values but sits some pixels higher
  on the plane in the pictures (`tests/crash_sea_near.txt`); cause
  not found.
- **Sky flash:** stepped every 3 VBLs here, per drawn frame on the Amiga (4 VBLs during a crash).
- **Rocket homing:** matches the Amiga at a pillbox; the ship gun path was only read. Our atan
  is a table search (can differ by 0.35 degrees), sin1024 truncates to degrees, the slip during the delay uses the
  direction at launch.
- **Game-over countdown** runs per tick (per drawn frame in the original).
- **Original quirks not reproduced:** the gun can hit falling planes and wrecks again (each hit scores +350 and
  counts as a kill, FUN_1b682 has no state test); a burning wreck on an island keeps the intact plane picture until
  it moves to the wreck list.
- **Front end:** the hires parts (briefing panel, marble slab) are halved to low resolution; table and name entry
  use the 5x7 message font in upper case; the night panel uses the night palette only (the Amiga's night dashboard
  picture differs in about 900 pixels).
- **World ends:** ours wraps at the tile map's sea margins, 200 px before either end; the original has a 16-bit x
  that wraps after about 65000 px of open sea.
- **Palette:** 16 colours for 32; a dark brown is forced in so that bunkers and huts keep their detail.
- **Ours only:** H (help page), Esc (pause page), Ctrl+Q (quit), a loading screen before every load, the title
  picture stays until the game is loaded.

## Not compared with the Amiga

- **Forward view** (ported from the code, `reverse-engineering/notes/forward_view.md`): the carrier shapes when flying left, the
  tree strip using `dug0` in the two nearest bands, the enemy-plane size table, the sticky "no landing view" flag
  after an enemy ship was shown. One capture with the own carrier ahead while flying left settles the first three.
  The window is 60 px wide here (61.5 on the Amiga).
- The J-carrier's take-off roll (ported, no test flight), the Zero's x-step helper in FUN_1d796, the launch routines
  11622 / 11510, the player's 1/8 frames.
- Saved games: the exact dialog texts, what else the original's file holds, the demo recording.

## Undecided

- **Frame pacing:** 3 VBLs per frame (16.7 fps, the Amiga's own rate) is the default.
- **Keys of ours** (H, Esc pause page, Ctrl+Q): keep per target or not.

## Enhancements (beyond the original, for a later edition)

- **Falcon030:** AGT's timer-driven display shows a black screen on the Videl; it would need a display path of its
  own. The game says "needs an STE or Mega STE" on Falcon and TT (the TT has no blitter).
- **1 MB machines:** about 665 KB too much today (1164 KB needed, 499 KB free). The level in memory (the map has
  4 bytes per cell), the screen buffers, sprites and sound would all have to shrink; an exact memory map of a
  running mission would be the first step.
- **Panel digits** as dark digits in white boxes (score, planes shot down), easier to read.
- **Propeller animation** (static in the original).

## Reference

**Builds** (`tools/make_release.sh` -> `builds/release-<id>/`): `hatari/` (unpacked, files beside the
program), `floppy/wof.st` (packed, one 720 KB disk, program in
AUTO, the data in `WOF.DAT`), `harddisk/WOF/` (`WOF.PRG` and the unpacked data in `WOF.DAT`). README.TXT with the build's
version line is in every target. Before publishing: run the floppy image on 2 MB, the files-beside-the-program
layout from a subfolder, and the hard disk version under HDDRIVER (an ACSI disk image with the HDDRIVER demo).

**Saved games:** `SAVE1.WOF` .. `SAVE6.WOF`, header + state blocks + the tile map entries that differ from the
mission's map (about 13 KB). Tied to the build: a change of a saved struct makes old files "not a saved game";
`SAVE_VERSION` must be raised when the meaning of a field changes.

**Footprint:** unpacked 5.7 MB (tiles 2.0, maps 2.7); packed floppy 720 KB image with about 95 KB free. The Amiga
original is 631 KB on its 880 KB disk.

**Speed:** 3 VBLs per frame (the pacing). The work per frame, measured in Hatari (`tools/hatari_frames.py`), is
about 2.0 VBLs on the deck and over the sea and 2.3 over a busy map (m); the rest is spare. Its biggest parts: the
sound mix 0.3 VBL with two voices playing (four voices: about 0.25 VBL for every VBL of sound), the sprites 0.3 to
0.45, the tile refill 0.25 to 0.35 (waves; a carrier bob step adds up to 0.7 for two frames), the per-frame effects
0.1 to 0.3, the entity tick 0.22, the forward view 0.1, the panel 0.02 (0.1 to 0.15 in a frame where an item
changes). Frames still go late where several of these peak together:
a bob step during the take-off roll, a ship sinking with four sounds, the later maps' ships and guns. Mixing at
6258 Hz would halve the sound's share but spoil the gun and splash samples (17 and 10 kHz).

**AGT:** the changes are in `agt-patch/agtools-local.patch` and described in `docs/AGT_CHANGES.md`. Known AGT fault to report some day: an IMSPR entity
in the same draw layer as EMX entities, or drawn last in a pass, makes the following EMX drawing crash (our
workaround: IMSPR only in layer 1, the EMX separator bar always last).

**Tests:** `tools/suite.sh <names>` replays `tests/*.txt` in Hatari (`WOF_MEMSIZE=2` for a
2 MB check). The Amiga side was run in a headless vAmiga with snapshots and scripted input (not part of this
repository).

fredangstadt-lang-linewarsii-sdl-readme-.text:
# LineWars II, portable

A playable reconstruction of the 1994 DOS game LineWars II, in portable C, targeting SDL3.

The engine here is not a lookalike. Every function was reconstructed from the original
game's machine code & then checked against it: 35 automated gates, 23 of which execute the
original 1994 binary inside an emulator & diff its return values, its VGA port writes & its
pixels against what our compiled C produces. Those gates run on any host, they came with the
code, & they are the contract this port has to keep.

![The demo at the 1280x960 display mode: the 3D scene at 2x internal detail](docs/captures/11_highres_1280x960.png)
![The attract intro at 640x480, the mode that stays byte-exact against the DOS build](docs/captures/07_intro.png)

## About this port

Native SDL3 port of the
[LineWars II reconstruction](https://github.com/fredangstadt-lang/LineWarsII-DOS).
That repo holds the full provenance, verification & how-it-was-made story.
LineWars II is © 1994 Patrick Aalto; the reconstruction is released as freeware
with his permission, and any commercial use requires a licensing discussion with
him.

The game core is the same verified C as the DOS build. Every hardware touch in
the reconstruction funnels through a small, closed set of leaf functions, so this
port is a new backend behind seams that already existed. That's why it went from
nothing to playable in an afternoon. The DOS build's platform-independent
gate suite runs against this build on the host.

Adds over the DOS build: high-resolution rendering, resizable window,
fullscreen. Builds on Linux and Windows (Windows binary cross-built under Linux,
tested via Proton).

Two porting bugs worth recording. The original depends on 32-bit integer
wraparound, & on LP64 Linux the un-wrapped value surfaced as a lighting bug: the
sun's position derives from the overflow. The other was filename
case-sensitivity. Both fixed & play-tested.

## Where this came from

The reconstruction was done in a separate repository,
<https://github.com/fredangstadt-lang/LineWarsII-DOS>, & that repo stays exactly as it is.
It holds the disassembly, the byte-offset annotations in every comment, the audit trail,
and the DOS build. **When something in this port behaves wrong, that repo is where you go
to find out what the original actually did.**

This repo holds the clean version: the same verified logic with the archaeology stripped
out, written to be read by someone who has never seen a 16-bit disassembler.

## Layout

    src/                 the engine, portable C
    include/             its headers
    platform/sdl3/       the SDL3 backend
    platform/dos_reference/hal_dos.c
                         the DOS backend, kept as the SPEC: every seam it answers,
                         the SDL backend has to answer too
    tests/gates/         the verification gates (verify_*.py + their C runners)
    tests/oracle/        the emulator harness that executes the original's bytes
    tests/unit/          host unit tests
    tools/               asset extractor, asset packer, test runner
    docs/                port notes, architecture, coverage, asset format
    reference/original/  original game material (Patrick Aalto's work, see below)
    assets/game.dat      the asset container (Patrick Aalto's work, see below)

## The port is a backend, not a rewrite

Every hardware touch in the engine funnels through a small, closed set of leaf functions.
The DOS backend answers them with INT 10h, INT 21h, VGA port writes and a Sound Blaster
DMA loop. The SDL3 backend answers the same calls with a texture, an audio stream and a
scancode queue. Nothing above the seam changes.

The seams are inventoried in `docs/SDL3_PORT_NOTES.md`, seam by seam, with the SDL3 call
that answers each one.

## Rules for code in this repo

The DOS repo is an archaeology site and reads like one. This one does not.

1. **No byte-offset archaeology in comments.** `/* @0x1d8f the scanline loop */` belongs
   in the other repo. A comment here says what the code does and why, not where it came
   from.
2. **No magic numbers.** Every constant gets a name that says what it means.
   `LW2_TRIG_SHIFT` and not `14`. `LW2_VGA_BYTES_PER_ROW` and not `80`.
3. **KNF style** (the OpenBSD conventions), consistently.
4. **The gates stay green.** Any cleanup that changes a gate's output is not a cleanup,
   it is a bug. Run `tools/run_unit_tests.sh` before and after.

## Original game material

The original game's files travel with this tree, redistributed as freeware with the
written permission of Patrick Aalto, the game's author (`NOTICE.md` has the terms):

- `reference/original/` - the original executable's code. The gates need it, because
  they run the real thing and diff our C against it.
- `assets/game.dat` - the art, music and mission text, repacked into our own container.

Both can be rebuilt from a copy of the game rather than taken on faith:
`tools/extract_assets.py` unpacks the original, and `tools/pack_gamedat.py` builds
`game.dat` from what it finds. Keep those tools working. They are how anyone else
reproduces the container, and how you regenerate it if the format changes.

## Status

The DOS build is complete & playable: all ten missions, byte-exact spawn tables, sound,
cockpit, radar, explosions. It runs at roughly 47 fps in missions under DOSBox-X, against the
original's 60.

The SDL3 build is playable end to end. `linewars2.exe` runs splash, menu, intro, flight,
debrief, the order screen & an in-game settings screen, with Sound Blaster Pro music & SFX
through `SDL_AudioStream`, keyboard & mouse control. It builds for Windows (WinLibs gcc
16.1.0 UCRT, or mingw-w64 cross-compiled from Linux) & natively for Linux; the INDEX8
texture path & the audio stream work on the software/opengl/vulkan drivers.

**Verified against the original, not against a screenshot:**

- The renderer: `tests/gates/test_gfx_runner_sdl.c` links the shipping SDL backend into the
  oracle harness & diffs it against the original VGADRV machine code executing in Unicorn:
  431 cases, 0 mismatches. `tools/run_unit_tests.sh` runs it on every invocation.
- The menu: byte-exact against the DOS `SHOT01.RAW` cell dump.
- Intro, flight & the demo: match the DOS reference captures (`docs/captures/`).
- Audio: the mixer is shared source with the DOS build; the captured PCM's level matches the
  DOS reference within ~10%.

Everything the player changes lives in a DOS-style tabbed settings screen (Graphics, Control,
Sound, Exit), reached from the menu's Configure row, saved to `settings.dat` next to the .exe:
the output resolution (640x480 up to 1920x1440, plus fullscreen), music & SFX volume, the 8x16
font, & every flight key rebound to any key or cleared. The resolution setting resizes the
window for real & renders the 3D at 2x internal detail past 640x480; at 2x the fonts, cockpit
sprites, gauge bars & radar blips all pixel-double to keep their size. 640x480 stays byte-exact
& keeps every gate green.

`docs/PORTING_CHECKLIST.md` is the plan & the status board; `docs/ROADMAP.md` lists the next
features (all-side missiles, LAN play, a custom-mission launcher); `docs/captures/` holds a shot
of each screen. `docs/SDL3_PORT_NOTES.md` is the underlying research, with an amendment box
marking what it got wrong.

## Building

SDL 3.4.12, built from source with the same compiler as the game (WinLibs gcc 16.1.0,
`x86_64-w64-mingw32`, UCRT). The official SDL mingw dev release is MSVCRT-built & mixing CRTs
is a bug hunt nobody needs.

    git clone --depth 1 --branch release-3.4.12 https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL.git
    cmake -S SDL -B SDL/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/path/to/SDL3 -DSDL_SHARED=ON -DSDL_STATIC=OFF \
        -DSDL_TESTS=OFF -DSDL_EXAMPLES=OFF
    cmake --build SDL/build --parallel && cmake --install SDL/build

Then the game (point `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` at wherever SDL3 was installed above):

    cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/SDL3
    cmake --build build

## The decisions behind the port

**We render our own 3D.** No GPU, no model conversion, no modern engine. SDL supplies a
window, a texture, an audio stream & an event queue. The game draws a few hundred flat,
untextured triangles a frame; software handles that in under a millisecond on any machine made
this century, & the fixed-point math is the part worth keeping.

**One chunky framebuffer.** The planar VGA address & the chunky pixel index are the same
number (`pixel = 4*off + plane`, derived in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`), so the port keeps every
verified rasterizer byte-for-byte & still gets a flat buffer, with no plane arrays & no
per-frame conversion.

**Pixel-exact at 320x480 first.** The engine renders into a 320x480 internal buffer (the
same 153,600 bytes every gate diffs) & the window shows it width-doubled at 640x480, which
is why the captures are 640x480. Higher resolution comes after, & only after, the
frozen-scene diff is clean. The 320x480 build is the oracle that proves the high-res one.

"""Steps 2-5 of the build (README): rebuild WIZARDS.EXE and MAGIC.EXE byte for byte and check them.

  python build.py --bc TOOLS --dosbox DOSBOX_X [--work WORK] [--parallel N]
      TOOLS     the folder that holds BORLANDC (install_bc31.py's OUT); mounted as C: in DOSBox-X
      DOSBOX_X  the dosbox-x executable
      WORK      the build folder (default: ./work); W/ and L/ get the objects and the executables
      N         DOSBox-X sessions at once (default 8)

Every compile runs in its OWN DOSBox-X session (`dosbox-x -silent`: no window, exits when its batch ends): Borland
C++ 3.1 reads leftovers of the previous run from memory, so compiles that share a session can differ. The Miles AIL
sound library is assembled from its released source (src/ail/) and linked as S2FC1.OBJ (WIZARDS.EXE) / AIL.OBJ
(MAGIC.EXE). No game file is read. Prints both executables' SHA-256 against the originals; exit status 0 when both
are identical."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.dirname(HERE)
ORIGINAL = {'WIZARDS.EXE': '83e273105b49ebb758b041c965298e45d491513e448e84ede2c6152232ad4e3d',
            'MAGIC.EXE': 'e9b96da031097fee92d8f00213f7406d5d22003c63e486b7f6394eaa078c3ebb'}
PROGRAMS = (('WIZARDS.EXE', 'W', 'WIZARDS.RSP', 'S2FC1.ASM'), ('MAGIC.EXE', 'L', 'MAGIC.RSP', 'AIL.ASM'))   # AIL's name


def overlays(rsp):
    """object files between /o and /o- of a response file: the modules compiled with -Y"""
    on, out = False, set()
    for line in open(rsp):
        for w in line.replace('+', ' ').split():
            if w == '/o':
                on = True
            elif w == '/o-':
                on = False
            elif on and w.upper().endswith('.OBJ'):
                out.add(w.upper())
    return out


def write_conf(path, tools, work, batch):
    open(path, 'w').write(
        '[dosbox]\nmemsize=16\n[cpu]\ncycles=max\ncore=normal\n[mixer]\nnosound=true\n[speaker]\npcspeaker=false\n'
        '[sblaster]\nsbtype=none\n[dos]\nxms=true\nems=false\n[autoexec]\nmount c "%s"\nmount d "%s"\nc:\n'
        'set PATH=C:\\BORLANDC\\BIN\nd:\ncall %s\nexit\n' % (os.path.abspath(tools), os.path.abspath(work), batch))


def run_sessions(dosbox, tools, work, batches, parallel):
    """each batch file in a fresh, silent DOSBox-X session, `parallel` at a time"""
    todo, running, t0 = list(batches), [], time.time()
    while todo or running:
        while todo and len(running) < parallel:
            b = todo.pop(0)
            conf = os.path.join(work, os.path.splitext(b)[0] + '.CNF')
            write_conf(conf, tools, work, b)
            running.append(subprocess.Popen([dosbox, '-silent', '-fastlaunch', '-nogui', '-conf', conf],
                                            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL))
        running = [p for p in running if p.poll() is None]
        time.sleep(0.2)
    return time.time() - t0


def module_files(prog):
    if prog == 'WIZARDS.EXE':
        d = os.path.join(REPO, 'src', 'wizards')
        return [os.path.join(d, f) for f in os.listdir(d) if f.upper().endswith(('.C', '.ASM'))]
    lines = open(os.path.join(REPO, 'src', 'magic', 'MODULES.TSV'), encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines()
    return [os.path.normpath(os.path.join(REPO, 'src', 'magic', l.split('\t')[1].strip()))
            for l in lines if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--bc', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--dosbox', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--work', default='work')
    ap.add_argument('--parallel', type=int, default=8)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    work = os.path.abspath(a.work)
    if os.path.isdir(work):
        shutil.rmtree(work)
    os.makedirs(work)
    # step 3: one folder per program, one fresh session per module
    batches = []
    for prog, folder, rsp, standin in PROGRAMS:
        d = os.path.join(work, folder)
        os.makedirs(d)
        for h in os.listdir(os.path.join(REPO, 'src', 'include')):
            shutil.copy(os.path.join(REPO, 'src', 'include', h), os.path.join(d, h.upper()))
        files = module_files(prog)
        for f in files:
            shutil.copy(f, os.path.join(d, os.path.basename(f).upper()))
        ail = os.path.join(REPO, 'src', 'ail')                  # step 2: the Miles AIL source
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(ail, 'AIL.ASM'), os.path.join(d, standin))
        for f in ('AIL.INC', 'AIL.MAC'):
            shutil.copy(os.path.join(ail, f), os.path.join(d, f))
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(HERE, rsp), os.path.join(d, rsp))
        ovl = overlays(os.path.join(HERE, rsp))
        for k, name in enumerate(sorted(os.path.basename(f).upper() for f in files) + [standin]):
            if name == standin:
                cmd = 'TASM /m /w+ /ml %s' % name                # AIL's own makefile flags (src/ail/README.txt)
            elif name.endswith('.ASM'):
                cmd = 'TASM /ml %s' % name
            else:
                y = '-Y ' if os.path.splitext(name)[0] + '.OBJ' in ovl else ''
                cmd = 'BCC %s-c -mm -a -d -IC:\\BORLANDC\\INCLUDE %s' % (y, name)
            bat = '%s%03d.BAT' % (folder, k)
            open(os.path.join(work, bat), 'w', newline='').write(
                'cd %s\r\n%s > %s%03d.LOG\r\ncd ..\r\n' % (folder, cmd, folder, k))
            batches.append(bat)
    t = run_sessions(a.dosbox, a.bc, work, batches, a.parallel)
    print('compiled %d modules in %.0f s' % (len(batches), t))
    # step 4: link at the original link date
    links = []
    for prog, folder, rsp, standin in PROGRAMS:
        bat = 'LINK%s.BAT' % folder
        open(os.path.join(work, bat), 'w', newline='').write(
            'cd %s\r\nDATE /F\r\nDATE 03/03/1995\r\nTLINK @%s > LINK.LOG\r\ncd ..\r\n' % (folder, rsp))
        links.append(bat)
    run_sessions(a.dosbox, a.bc, work, links, 2)
    # step 5: compare with the originals
    ok = True
    for prog, folder, rsp, standin in PROGRAMS:
        p = os.path.join(work, folder, prog)
        h = hashlib.sha256(open(p, 'rb').read()).hexdigest() if os.path.exists(p) else 'missing'
        ok = ok and h == ORIGINAL[prog]
        print('%-12s %s  %s' % (prog, h, 'IDENTICAL to v1.31' if h == ORIGINAL[prog] else 'DIFFERS'))
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# The Anger of Pharaoh XXXV — reverse-engineered file formats

Everything below was recovered from `GAME.EXE` (Borland C++ 4, 16-bit real mode, 74 516 bytes,
January 1997) by disassembly, and from the data files that ship next to it. Offsets given as
`07bb:xxxx` are code-segment offsets inside the EXE; they match the comments in `src/engine.js`.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GAME.DAT` | The whole game: palette, verb table, 6 room pictures, 67 object records (names, sprites, script). |
| `CHAR.DAT` | 91 glyphs of an 8×12 font, ASCII 32..122. |
| `BEGIN.GFX` | Title picture, 320×100 drawn at y=20. |
| `END.GFX` | Ending picture, 320×100 drawn at y=90. |
| `END1.GFX` … `END5.GFX` | Five random "you are dead" panels, 164×70 drawn at (78,55). |

All numbers are little-endian. Every picture uses the same layout, which the engine calls with a
single blit routine (`07bb:2d52`, opaque copy):

```
word height, word width, word x, word y, then height*width bytes, one palette index per pixel
```

## Video

Mode 13h (320×200×256). The room picture occupies rows 0..99, the text console rows 109..199
(seven 13-pixel lines; the console scrolls with `07bb:3032`). Text is drawn with the CHAR.DAT
glyphs at colour index `0x1C`; the underline cursor uses index 15. Menu boxes use index 249 (red)
or 252 (blue). Palette values in `GAME.DAT` are 8-bit and are divided by 4 before being
programmed into the DAC (`07bb:0150`). Screen changes fade through black in 64 palette steps,
one per vertical retrace (`07bb:2e17`).

## CHAR.DAT

91 records of 100 bytes: `word 12, word 8`, then 96 pixel bytes (row-major, `0x1C` = ink,
`0` = paper). Record *n* is ASCII 32+*n*.

## GAME.DAT

```
0   "DS"
2   dword verb table size          (203)
6   dword verb table offset
10  dword palette offset           (768 bytes, 8-bit RGB)
14  word  screen count             (6)
16  word  object count             (67)
18  dword runtime object table offset
22  (screens + objects) × { word, dword offset }   -- 73 directory entries
```

The word in each directory entry is a size hint; only the offset matters. Screens come first
(each a 320×100 picture, 32 008 bytes), then the objects.

**Runtime object table** (`object count` × 6 bytes at offset 18's target): `word SCR` (room the
object is in), `word FLG`, `word CDT` (condition/state, starts at 0). This table is copied into
memory at start-up and mutated by the script. FLG bits:

| bit | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0x01 | record loaded in memory (object is in the current room or in the inventory) |
| 0x02 | carried in the inventory |
| 0x04 | any redraw of this object repaints the whole room |
| 0x08 | invisible (sprite not drawn) |
| 0x10 | cannot be referred to by name yet |
| 0x20 | never loaded even if carried (unused by the data) |

**Verb table**: NUL-separated synonyms, groups separated by an empty string, `0xFF` at the end.
Group numbers are 1-based: 1 LOOK, 2 USE, 3 TAKE, 4 EXAMINE, 5 USE…WITH, 6 OPEN, 7 CLOSE, 8 GO.
A `0xFE` inside a synonym (`USE\xFEWITH`, `PUT\xFEIN`) marks a two-part verb whose second half
is matched after the first object.

### Object record

```
0   word  n            number of extra sprite slots
2   dword cmd          offset (from record start) of the script block
6   dword sprite[0]    sprite for condition 0 (0 = none)
10  dword sprite[1..n] sprites for conditions 1..n
    names: NUL-terminated synonyms, terminated by an empty string (first one is the display name)
    sprites and script follow
```

The sprite shown for an object is `sprite[CDT]`. The first name is printed by the inventory box.

### Script block

```
cmd+0   word nblocks
cmd+2   nblocks × word   offsets (from cmd) of each verb block
block:  word verb, dword obj2, then entries { word proc, dword data offset (from record start) }
        terminated by proc = 0
```

A verb block is selected by `(verb, obj2)`; `obj2` is the second object of a two-part command
(0 otherwise). Entries run in order; each internal procedure returns 0 (next entry), 1 (restart
the block), -1 (stop), or 2 (restart the whole game). Procedures are called through a table of
far pointers at `DS:03FE`, indexed by `(proc-1)*4`, so a bad number prints "Reference to non
existing internal function".

### Internal procedures

| # | data | effect |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | obj, cond | Set CDT; erase the old sprite by restoring the room background under it and draw the new one (skipped when hidden, carried, or not loaded). Used for animations with 41. |
| 4 | obj, mask | FLG &= mask, then redraw the sprite if bits 2 or 8 changed. |
| 5 | obj, mask | FLG \|= mask, same redraw rule. |
| 6 | obj, mask | FLG ^= mask, same redraw rule. |
| 7 | screen | Unload everything and enter a room (-1 = reload the current one). Returns -1. |
| 8 | obj, screen | Move an object to another room. |
| 20 | text | Print (`\n` = next line, `\r` = carriage return). |
| 30 | obj, cond, n, n×{proc, off} | If `CDT[obj] == cond` run the nested procedures ("in_p_ifcee"). |
| 31 | same | If `CDT[obj] != cond` run the nested procedures. |
| 39 | – | Lightning: fade the palette to white, wait 2 s, fade back. |
| 40 | dialogue node | Multiple-choice dialogue (see below). |
| 41 | ms | Delay. |
| 42 | – | Random death panel with Retry (returns 1) / Forget it (returns 2). |
| 43 | – | The ending; returns 2. |

Procedures 32–34 exist in the EXE (flag tests) but are never used by the data.

### Dialogue node (procedure 40)

```
text NUL
word nprocs, nprocs × { word proc, 20 bytes data }   (only death nodes use this: proc 42)
byte nanswers
nanswers × answer text NUL
nanswers × word offset of the child node, relative to THIS node
```

Answers are shown as `1)…`, `2)…` and chosen with the digit keys. The whole tree lives inside the
ROCK object (id 54) and is entered by `USE ROCK WITH SOCKET` in the last room.

## Parser (`07bb:14ad`)

The input line is normalised in place (letters upper-cased, runs of spaces collapsed, one space
appended). The verb is the longest synonym that prefixes the line and is followed by a space
(earlier synonyms win ties); the object is the longest name of any *loaded, nameable* object that
follows it. If text remains, the line is parsed again allowing only two-part verbs, whose second
half (`WITH`, `IN`, `ON`) must precede the second object. Error messages are drawn at random from
four tables: empty line, unknown verb, unknown object, malformed sentence. A sentence that parses
but has no matching block gets one of five "You can't do that here" style replies.

## Input loop (`07bb:26c9`)

A 20-line doskey history (60 bytes each, at most 39 characters typed), Home/End/arrows/Ins/Del
editing, F1 help, F2/F3 print SAVE/LOAD and do nothing else, F4/Esc options menu, F5 inventory,
F10/Ctrl-X/Alt-X quit. Invalid keys beep at a random pitch; more than ten in a row print a random
"Stop playing with that…" message.
